A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R2R work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original R2R benchmark results, latency measurements, router ablations, and routing analyses, including Tables 2–6 and Figures 4–8.

after.justification: v2 retains original R2R experiments and adds human-verifier comparisons, generalization experiments, efficiency and failure analyses, and stochastic-decoding results.

M1.justification: The core router and greedy routing procedure remain unchanged. Appendix C.1 adds a stochastic variant that samples initial predictions while retaining deterministic continuations for practical labeling; B.4.2 adds query-level selection between two R2R systems. These are bounded procedural extensions. The five-to-six-layer correction in Section 4.3 does not establish an architecture change: v1 Appendix A.1 already specifies six layers.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluation on Arena-Hard dialogue and MMLU-Redux-Philosophy, substantially extending coverage beyond the retained mathematics, coding, and science-QA benchmarks. Appendix B.1 also adds a human-annotated evaluation of semantic-divergence judgments.

E2.justification: The original main-table comparators remain, but v2 substantially expands evaluated comparisons with Qwen3 dense models and the Qwen3-30BA3B MoE baseline. Its new verifier comparison includes a human annotator and Qwen2.5-7B/3B alongside Qwen2.5-72B. RSD is added only to related work, not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: New protocols include majority/unanimous human-label ground truths, cross-LLM router transfer, an easy/hard AIME partition, and stochastic generation/evaluation at temperature 0.6 and top-p 0.95 with a separate 16.1M-token labeling dataset. Section 5.4 now explicitly adjusts ablation thresholds, replacing v1's statement that other settings were fixed. The batch-size 2/4 speculative-decoding evaluation is removed.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct verifier validation and verifier-quality sensitivity, continuation-length sensitivity, cross-LLM transfer, SLM-size ablations, recall-versus-routing-rate curves, runtime and activation-interval analyses, and systematic failure analysis. These test assumptions largely unexamined in v1. Conversely, v1 Appendix B.1's speculative-decoding batch-scaling analysis is removed.

E5.justification: Appendix C.1.3 newly reports stochastic AIME pass@1 over 16 independent samples per problem. This documents repetition for an added experiment, without establishing additional runs of the original experiments. The existing across-question standard deviations and routing-percentile bands remain.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 retain their values, but Table 4's Different variant changes from 19.7K tokens, 14.4% LLM usage, and 333 seconds to 21.0K, 13.1%, and 228 seconds alongside the revised threshold protocol. v2 adds extensive verifier, generalization, efficiency, failure, and sampling results, including 58% sampled AIME pass@1 at 8.6B parameters. It removes the multi-batch results and corrects Section 3.2's 3% usage attribution from the SLM to the LLM.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1.1 introduces a probabilistic divergence-threshold formulation and asserts expected-quality preservation when calibrated to LLM self-divergence. This is new mathematical content, although no corresponding proof is supplied. The original deterministic definitions, equations, and Appendix E quality-guarantee proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims about divergence-based labeling, immediate token routing, and improved performance-efficiency trade-offs. Headline claims, including 5.6B average parameters and approximately 2.8-fold generation-speed improvement, remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of verifier reliability, transfer between model pairs, memory-traffic savings, and complementary trade-offs with MoE. It identifies sentence-reordering false positives and repetitive reasoning that exhausts the token budget as limitations. The conclusion replaces the greedy-only limitation with a qualification that alternative sampling has received limited validation.

D1.justification: v2 documents the sampling implementation, including k=1, divergence threshold 0.5, and deterministic continuations after sampled predictions. It reconciles the main-text layer count with the existing architecture appendix. Conversely, it drops v1's explicit speculative draft-tree depth and expansion-node settings. Most Appendix A implementation details, training hyperparameters, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds nine references, including high-entropy-token research, RSD, new benchmark sources, and efficiency-analysis sources. It extends discussion of reward-guided routing, task-specific verification, and compatibility with MoE and query-level routing. The central positioning around immediate semantic-divergence correction and most existing related-work discussion remain intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative are retained. Changes include copyediting, updated conference and funding text, a shorter conclusion, and renaming Section 5.3 to Efficiency. Appendix results are regrouped; the former routing-algorithm appendix moves into C.2, and related work moves from C to D. Much of the expansion consists of new scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 adds numerous tables and three new analysis figures covering verifier checks, generalization, efficiency, compatibility, failures, and sampling. Table 4 gains a recall column and reordered fields; the old batch-scaling table disappears. Existing displays are also relocated: v1 Figure 7 becomes v2 Figure 11, and Table 6 becomes Table 9 without substantive content changes.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct human validation of its semantic labels and systematic failure analysis. v2 addresses both and tests verifier quality, continuation length, and transfer across tasks and models, substantially strengthening evidence for the central routing assumptions and clarifying practical limits. These gains outweigh the removal of multi-batch baseline evidence and associated implementation details. The stochastic extension is useful, although its expected-quality guarantee remains asserted without a new proof.
